config.detail: No config.json on HF. The release safetensors carries its config as JSON metadata (format=sava); it equals the SavaConfig defaults: hidden 512, ffn 2048, rms_eps 1e-6, layers [mamba, mamba, mamba, attention], Mamba-2 expand 2 / head_dim 64 / state 128 / groups 1 / conv 4 / chunk 64, attention 8 heads / 2 kv heads / head_dim 64 / window 512 / rope_theta 1e4 / xsa alpha 1, vad and turn branches hidden 512 / ffn 1536 with the same attention, turn_horizons [0, 5, 10, 20], vad_embed_size 64, lookahead_frames 3, mixer_context_frames 2, log_energy_floor 1e-5.

preprocessor.detail: Causal Whisper-style log-mel: 240 zero samples of left context, 400-sample periodic-Hann DFT every 160 samples (window ends where its hop ends), power, 128 Slaney mel bins (0-8 kHz), log10(max(x, 1e-10)), (x + 4) / 4, no max-8 clamp. A 640-sample frame is its 4 hops hop-major (512 values) plus ln(max(rms(frame), 1e-5)).

safetensors_metadata.detail: 77 tensors, all bfloat16, 25,521,558 parameters; sha256 aa610ee9b5d3d1be96f70581a8a3affe7cf20d06816b4ada1efdd8ab6274be34 (pinned in inworld.sava.registry). HF's safetensors-metadata API does not report it.

reference_modeling_code.detail: Upstream's own package; PyPI 1.0.0 is byte-identical to https://github.com/inworld-ai/sava tag v1.0.0 (commit b4221a54458ea60df8c777911d0567418994cacc). Its golden test (tests/fixtures/speech_expected.npz, atol 2e-4) passes in scripts/envs/sava.

dtype.evidence: Weights are stored bfloat16; inworld.sava.checkpoint.load upcasts them to fp32 on CPU and every reference run (golden fixture, benchmarks on A100 fp32) is fp32. bf16 -> fp32 is exact, so the F32 GGUF holds exactly the reference's weights. BF16 is the source dtype and a lossless size option for Stage 5.

upstream_benchmarks.dataset: Inworld VAD suite (nine public dataset readings) and end-of-turn clip sets
upstream_benchmarks.notes: Publisher reports frame AUC for voice activity (vs Silero VAD) and clip AUC for end of turn (vs smart-turn v3.2), per dataset, no combined score. Not a port contract. Acceptance is per-frame probability parity and exact turn-segment parity with inworld.sava.run / sava.segment; there is no WER.

reference_rationale: Inworld publishes the model only with its own plain-PyTorch package (no HF config, no transformers class). inworld.sava.run (whole recording = Session push + flush) and Session are the canonical inference paths; sava.segment / TurnSegmenter with the default Policy is the reference turn rule. Pinned to inworld-sava 1.0.0 (git v1.0.0, b4221a5) on torch 2.14.1, fp32, CPU, 1 thread, weights inworld/sava@1beae7c1.
known_risks: New TURN role (docs/turn.md) plus the VAD role with lookahead: acceptance is per-frame speech / turn probability parity and exact turn-segment parity with sava.segment, not WER.

Streaming, causal, stateful: mel context (240 samples), mixer tail (1 row), 3 Mamba-2 conv tails + SSM states, 3 sliding-window KV caches (512 frames), the previous frame's speech probability, and the frame counter. Frames must be processed in order.

Lookahead: the released speech probability of frame t is emitted at step t + 3; steps 0..2 emit NO_SPEECH_LOGIT (-30). Flush pads the partial frame with zeros, then steps 3 frames of silence; their turn scores (flush_turns) feed sava.segment.
run == push(all) + flush only up to rounding in the reference (<= 3.1e-6 in probability): offline uses the chunked SSD scan and 512-frame attention windows, streaming the per-frame recurrence.

RoPE uses absolute fp32 positions that never reset within a stream: the reference's own outputs drift with stream age (speech max 3.3e-5 at 5 min, 4.2e-4 at 1 h, 3e-3 at 11 h vs the same audio at position 0), though the model is mathematically shift invariant. ggml_rope's iterated theta_scale does not reproduce torch's per-index frequencies.

Mamba-2 maps onto ggml_ssm_conv / ggml_ssm_scan (A {1, n_head}); the conv kernel and A must be F32 for those ops; dt softplus happens inside ggml_ssm_scan; the D skip, gating and grouped RMSNorm are separate ops.
Exclusive self attention (XSA) removes each head's projection on its own frame's value: no ggml op; built from mul / sum_rows.
Turn head depends on sigmoid(previous step's on-time speech logit): the turn branch is sequential across frames in a stream (offline it is a one-step shift of the VAD head output).
sava.segment turns may overlap (a closed turn ends at decision step + 1, up to 3 frames past the judged frame; the next turn's 800 ms pre-roll is not clamped) and include dropped (kept=false) turns.
Segment parity is threshold-sensitive on long audio: on dots-full a pause-frame turn score sits 2.9e-6 from 0.9.
Weights are bf16; the reference computes in fp32. F32 GGUF is the parity artifact; BF16 is lossless storage but bf16 matmuls would not be.
